bull_bear.body: Dividend recommended INR 0.50/share based on Adjusted PAT of INR 668 Cr. Focus on deleveraging post-major Nagaur capex; no immediate M&A; potential JV buyout in UAE in 2-3 years.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical tension in West Asia impacting fuel/packing bag costs; Regulatory delays for Punjab plant (EC approval); Labor shortages in key Southern states; GGBS slag supply dependency on JSW Steel contracts.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Optimistic on long-term demand and North India traction; Prudent on accounting (expensing launch costs); Nimble regarding capacity reallocation (Rajasthan vs. Punjab); Confident in cost leadership via ESG/green energy.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly expensed INR 23 Cr North India launch costs rather than capitalizing them to adhere to 'prudent accounting,' artificially depressing Q4 margins despite minimal revenue contribution from Nagaur in the quarter. The Punjab plant delay has triggered a strategic pivot to double down on Rajasthan grinding capacity (6 MT total) rather than waiting, utilizing existing limestone reserves for potential future clinker lines there.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Long-term credit rating upgraded to IND AA- (from IND A+, Stable outlook) by India Ratings and Research.
- Net Debt/EBITDA (TTM) and Net Debt/Equity both improved sharply from a year earlier, indicating a deleveraging balance sheet even as the large capex program (up to 68.3 MTPA grinding potential) continues to ramp.
- Deck does not disclose an explicit dividend policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Largest manufacturer of GGBS in India, with leadership in slag-based/blended low-carbon cement
- Secured raw-material linkages: blast furnace slag, fly ash and by-product fuel gases sourced from co-located JSW Steel and JSW Energy plants
- Strategically located plants across multiple regions, with the Nagaur plant marking entry into northern India
- Extensive sales and distribution network — 7,900+ dealers, 257 distribution points, 4,600+ sub-dealers and 7,500 direct non-trade customers
- One of the lowest CO2 emission intensities in the cement industry (269 kg/tcm Scope 1+2), supporting a cost and sustainability advantage
- Strong corporate lineage and ecosystem synergies as part of the JSW Group
- Among India's fastest-growing cement manufacturers by grinding capacity and sales volume CAGR (FY2016-FY2026)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Client/customer concentration — The Company's own forward-looking-statement disclosure explicitly flags 'client concentration' as a risk factor that could cause actual results to differ materially from expectations.
- Intense competition within the cement industry — Management flags intense competition within the cement industry, including factors that may affect the Company's cost advantage, as a risk to results.
- Execution risk on the multi-site capacity-expansion pipeline — The Company explicitly flags its ability to commission mines and new plants within contemplated time and cost, and its ability to raise finance within time and cost, as risks — material given its stated vision of reaching 60 MTPA capacity through a large greenfield/brownfield pipeline (Nagaur ramp-up, Vijayanagar, Dolvi, Punjab, UAE, Hatta in Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh).
- Talent attraction/retention and wage inflation — The Company flags its ability to attract and retain highly skilled professionals, and wage increases in India, as risks that could affect its ability to manage growth.
- Withdrawal of fiscal/governmental incentives and regulatory change — Management explicitly flags withdrawal of fiscal/governmental incentives and the impact of regulatory measures as risk factors to results.
- Acquisition integration and JV/associate performance risk — The Company flags its ability to successfully complete and integrate potential acquisitions, and the success of companies in which it has made strategic investments (joint ventures/associates), as risks to consolidated performance.
- Short-term liquidity position — The Current Ratio stood at 0.72 as of 31 March 2026 (versus 0.65 a year earlier) — current liabilities continued to exceed current assets even after the IPO-driven balance-sheet strengthening.
- Cross-border political, legal and immigration risk from international operations — Management flags political instability, legal restrictions on raising capital or acquiring companies outside India, and restrictions on immigration as risk factors, relevant given the Company's UAE operations (JSW Cement FZC and the newly incorporated JSW Cement Mideast LLC-SPC) and planned overseas grinding capacity.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- Part of JSW Group, a ~US$25bn Indian conglomerate spanning steel, energy, ports, paints and mobility, providing raw material, power, logistics and brand synergies plus customer trust.
- Among India's fastest-growing cement manufacturers with a multi-region footprint across South, West, East and North India, plus UAE.
- India's single largest manufacturer of GGBS, with ~84% all-India GGBS market share, 9,800+ active dealers and 7,500+ direct customers.
- Lowest CO2 emission intensity in the Indian cement industry (268 kg/ton, FY26), 52% below Indian peers and 50% below global peers.

business.body:

outlook.body: Volume Growth: Mid-to-high teens for FY27 (excluding North); North Plant Utilization: 50-60% for FY27; Capex: INR 2,300 Cr (FY27), INR 2,200 Cr (FY28); Margin Trajectory: Improving via INR 100/ton cost savings over FY27-FY28.

outlook.body: Not applicable for cement sector; demand visibility tied to infrastructure/housing projects in South & West India, with new pipeline developing in Rajasthan/Haryana.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Nagaur expansion: Additional 2.5 MT grinding capacity approved (total 6 MT by Q4 FY28) to offset Punjab delays; UAE grinding unit commissioning delayed to April 2027; Potential second clinker line in Rajasthan pending Punjab EC status.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Creating a pan-India footprint through new plants and targeted expansions in existing regions, de-risking execution via early action on land, mining rights and approvals
- Deepening presence in existing and new markets by strengthening distribution reach, brand investments, premium offerings and digital/dealer engagement tools
- Digital transformation across operations — AI-led energy optimisation, a Model Digital Plant, automated despatch, real-time logistics visibility, enhanced dealer platforms and Agentic AI for efficiency and customer experience
- Sustainability positioned as a core product and operating advantage, anchored in the CO-CREATE ESG framework, with a next-generation set of ESG targets being developed for publication
- Disciplined, demand-visibility- and cost-efficiency-led capital allocation across expansion, operations and product development
- Maintaining leadership in GGBS and green/blended cementitious products to capture the industry's shift toward lower-embodied-carbon construction materials
- Following its August 2025 IPO listing, the Board recommended the Company's first dividend of Rs 0.50 per equity share (face value Rs 10) for FY 2025-26, payable out of free reserves, to be put to Members for declaration at the 20th AGM. Board governance processes include a structured annual Board Evaluation Policy covering the performance of Directors, Committees and the Board as a whole, and a framework for the Board to regularly review key strategic and tactical risks and mitigation status.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: JSW Cement commissioned its greenfield integrated cement plant at Nagaur, Rajasthan during FY 2025-26 (Q4 FY26) — its first facility in North India — with 3.30 MTPA clinkerisation capacity and an initial 2.50 MTPA cement grinding capacity, taking consolidated clinker capacity to 9.74 MTPA and grinding capacity to 24.1 MTPA. Shiva Cement, the listed subsidiary, commissioned a 1.0 MTPA grinding unit at Sambalpur, Odisha, strengthening the eastern India presence. Looking ahead, the Company expects an additional 1.0 MTPA grinding unit at Nagaur to commence operations in FY 2026-27, and plans further grinding-capacity expansions at Vijayanagar, Karnataka (from 6.0 MTPA to 8.0 MTPA), Dolvi, Maharashtra (from 4.5 MTPA to 8.5 MTPA) and Nagaur, Rajasthan (from 3.5 MTPA to 6.0 MTPA). It has incorporated a wholly-owned subsidiary, JSW Cement Mideast LLC-SPC, to build a 1.65 MTPA cement grinding unit in the UAE, targeted for commercial start-up in FY 2027-28. Management has articulated a longer-term target of 46.0 MTPA grinding and about 13 MTPA clinker capacity, alongside plans to enter Central India, building on an existing base across South, West and East India plus the newly entered North India market. Capex incurred during FY 2025-26 was stated at Rs 1,947 crore in the narrative sections (Value Created Across Capitals), funded through a mix of IPO proceeds, internal accruals and disciplined debt management. Sustainability-linked capacity additions are also underway: 149 MW of renewable energy capacity and 19 MW of additional waste heat recovery system (WHRS) capacity, against an installed renewable base of 34.7 MW and installed WHRS of 36 MW (including JSW FZC) as at 31 March 2026. Raw-material security for the expansion pipeline is being reinforced via the Sikilangsho limestone block acquisition in Assam and rights/letters of intent over seven other mines across Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Assam.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Infrastructure-led demand: public capital expenditure on roads, railways, metros, airports, logistics parks and urban infrastructure expected to keep supporting cement consumption
- Housing remains the largest demand driver; increased Union Budget FY 2026-27 allocations for PMAY-Urban and PMAY-Rural support both urban and rural construction demand
- India's construction ecosystem is shifting toward blended cement and supplementary cementitious materials, which the company says aligns directly with its slag-based product strategy
- Cost volatility from global supply disruptions, West Asia tensions and energy price pressure is raising imported fuel, freight, packing and logistics costs, making operational efficiency critical for margin protection
- Indian cement industry volumes projected by CRISIL Intelligence to grow 6.5-7.5% in FY 2027 to reach ~533 million tonnes, supported by continued infrastructure-led government spending
- Regional demand in the company's own markets reflected roads, irrigation, expressways, housing and urban infrastructure activity
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: JSW Cement successfully commissioned its strategic Nagaur plant in March 2026, marking entry into North India, though Q4 margins were impacted by one-off North launch costs and temporary GGBS supply disruptions at Dolvi. The company maintains a mid-to-high teens volume growth guidance for FY27, underpinned by a robust cost-reduction roadmap targeting INR100/ton savings through green energy adoption and logistics optimization.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A leading Indian manufacturer of green, low-carbon and blended cement, and the country's largest producer of GGBS, built on secured slag/fly-ash linkages with the JSW Group and an extensive pan-India distribution network.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: JSW Cement manufactures clinker, cement (including blended Portland Slag Cement and other low-carbon products), GGBS (ground granulated blast furnace slag), ready-mix concrete (RMC) and construction chemicals, sold to individual home builders, contractors, infrastructure developers and institutional customers across India. Several plants draw blast furnace slag, fly ash and by-product fuel gases directly from co-located JSW Steel and JSW Energy plants, underpinning a circular, low-carbon manufacturing model.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest manufacturer of GGBS in India, with leadership in slag-based/blended low-carbon cement
- Secured raw-material linkages: blast furnace slag, fly ash and by-product fuel gases sourced from co-located JSW Steel and JSW Energy plants
- Strategically located plants across multiple regions, with the Nagaur plant marking entry into northern India
- Extensive sales and distribution network — 7,900+ dealers, 257 distribution points, 4,600+ sub-dealers and 7,500 direct non-trade customers
- One of the lowest CO2 emission intensities in the cement industry (269 kg/tcm Scope 1+2), supporting a cost and sustainability advantage
- Strong corporate lineage and ecosystem synergies as part of the JSW Group
- Among India's fastest-growing cement manufacturers by grinding capacity and sales volume CAGR (FY2016-FY2026)

The Punjab plant delay has triggered a strategic pivot to double down on Rajasthan grinding capacity (6 MT total) rather than waiting, utilizing existing limestone reserves for potential future clinker lines there.

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.
